The final response must provide: (1) Capability purpose section outline, (2) Configuration options outline, and (3) Example usage outline. No files should be modified.\n\nConstraints\n- The planner subagent may use bash\/search for discovery.\n- Parent execution may use only read_file.\n- Do not modify any files.\n- Keep the final response under 180 words.\n- Execute only the analysis part of the plan after planning.\n\nExpected Outcomes\n- A realistic implementation plan for a small docs update.\n- A concise, analysis-only proposal summarizing the three requested outlines.\n- The proposal should reflect repository-specific terminology where possible, based on discovered docs\/content.\n\nAcceptance Criteria\n- Plan includes clear steps for discovery, analysis, and drafting.\n- Final response contains exactly the three requested outline sections.\n- No code or file changes are made.\n- Final response remains under 180 words."}"}}]},{"role":"tool","tool_call_id":"call_T1hfjSLC3UungU4EP0q4U0OR","content":"1	# Key Reference Files
     2	
     3	## Monorepo Root
     4	
     5	- **CONTRIBUTING.md** - Development workflows, package management, and contribution guidelines
     6	- **CONTENTS.md** - Project structure and package overview
     7	- **README.md** - Main project documentation
     8	- **HARD REFERENCE** - `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the source of truth for QA execution (`composer qa`, `qa:*`) and contribution workflow details.
     9	
    10	## Individual Subpackages
    11	
    12	Each package in `packages/` may contain:
    13	- **README.md** - Package-specific documentation
    14	- **OVERVIEW.md** - Package overview and architecture
    15	- **INTERNALS.md** - Implementation details and internal structure
    16	- **CHEATSHEET.md** - Quick reference for package usage
    17	
    18	# Code Style
    19	
    20	- Use strict types and type hints for arguments and return values everywhere
    21	- Do not nest control structures (if, loops) beyond 1 level, exceptionally 2 levels
    22	- Use `match` for complex conditionals - avoid `if`/`else if` chains or `switch` statements; avoid ternary operators
    23	- Prefer immutable data structures and functional programming paradigms
    24	- Avoid using arrays as collections - use dedicated collection classes
    25	- Avoid exceptions for control flow - do not wrap everything in try/catch; either let exceptions bubble up or use monadic Cognesy\Utils\Result\Result for error handling if error needs to be handled on the same level
    26	- Use namespaces and PSR-4 autoloading
    27	
    28	## Agents Package Style
    29	
    30	- Data classes are `readonly final class` — all properties readonly, all mutations return new instances via `with*()` methods
    31	- Interfaces use `Can-` prefix (`CanUseTools`, `CanEmitAgentEvents`, `CanInterceptAgentLifecycle`)
    32	- Hooks use `Hook` suffix (`StepsLimitHook`, `ErrorPolicyHook`)
    33	- Accessors have no prefix: `state()`, `execution()`, `currentStep()` — not `getState()`
    34	- Mutators use `with` prefix and return `self`: `withState()`, `withCurrentStep()`
    35	- Named constructors for defaults: `::empty()`, `::fresh()`; for hydration: `::fromArray()`
    36	- Minimal docblocks — only on class/interface declarations; methods are self-documenting via types and naming
    37	- Method order: constructors → lifecycle/transitions → accessors → mutators → private helpers → serialization (`toArray`/`fromArray`)
    38	- Enums are string-backed for serialization; put logic (priority, comparison) as methods on the enum itself
    39	- Use `match(true) { ... }` for multi-condition branching
    40	- Use `$this->field ?? Default::empty()` pattern ("ensure pattern") to provide defaults instead of null-checking
    41	
    42	# Design Principles
    43	
    44	- Always start with extremely simple code, refactor when it is required - do not over-engineer solutions (YAGNI)
    45	- Use DDD (Domain Driven Design) principles - aggregate roots, value objects, entities, repositories, services
    46	- Use Clean Code and SOLID principles
    47	- Use interfaces for contracts, avoid concrete class dependencies
    48	- Prefer using monadic designs for complex fragments of code - e.g. to avoid null checks and make the code cleaner and simpler.
    49	
    50	## Agents Package Architecture
    51	
    52	### Mental Model
    53	
    54	- **AgentLoop** is a step-based iterator: each step = one LLM inference + tool execution cycle
    55	- Loop lifecycle: `beforeExecution` → [`beforeStep` → `handleToolUse` → `afterStep` → check `shouldStop()`]* → `afterExecution`
    56	- The loop yields intermediate states via `iterate()` (generator pattern) — callers can observe/persist between steps
    57	
    58	### State Layering
    59	
    60	- **AgentState** = session-level (persistent across executions): agentId, messages, metadata, optional `ExecutionState`
    61	- **ExecutionState** = transient per-run: executionId, status, steps, continuation signals — null between executions
    62	- **AgentStep** = immutable snapshot of one step: input/output messages, inference response, tool executions, errors
    63	- **StepExecution** = wraps AgentStep with timing and continuation metadata — keeps step data immutable while tracking execution details
    64	- State updates are always atomic — `withCurrentStepCompleted()` chains through the layers to prevent partial/inconsistent states
    65	- `AgentLoop` auto-resets terminal executions (completed/failed) on entry — no manual `forNextExecution()` needed
    66	
    67	### Stop/Continuation
    68	
    69	- **StopSignal** = value object with reason (enum) + message + context + source
    70	- **StopReason** enum has priority ordering for conflict resolution (ErrorForbade > StopRequested > StepsLimitReached > ...)
    71	- **ExecutionContinuation** aggregates stop signals; `shouldStop()` = has signals AND no continuation override
    72	- **AgentStopException** is a control-flow exception (not an error) — caught in loop, converted to StopSignal
    73	
    74	### Invariant vs Variant Behavior
    75	
    76	The boundary between `\Core` and `\Hook` is **whether the behavior is optional**:
    77	
    78	- **Core state transitions** = invariant. Always happens, can't be removed, not configurable. Folded into `with*()` methods on state objects. Examples: `withCurrentStep()` routes step output to the correct message section; `withCurrentStepCompleted()` archives the step; `AgentLoop.ensureNextExecution()` auto-resets terminal executions on entry.
    79	- **Hooks** = variant. Configurable, optional, composable via builder. Examples: step limits, token limits, summarization, finish reason stopping. If you could imagine an agent that doesn't need it, it's a hook.
    80	
    81	**State transitions must be complete.** Every `with*()` call leaves the state fully consistent — no follow-up call required. If behavior always follows a transition, fold it into that transition. A separate "remember to also call X" method implies the behavior is optional; if it isn't optional, the separation is wrong.
    82	
    83	**The litmus test:** if you're writing a hook that always runs, can't be removed, and has ordering dependencies with other hooks — it's a missing state transition, not a hook.
    84	
    85	**AgentLoop is domain-agnostic.** It orchestrates lifecycle phases (beforeStep → handleToolUse → afterStep → shouldStop) but has zero knowledge of message sections, buffer routing, or output formats. Domain behavior lives in state objects (invariant) or hooks (variant), never in the loop.
    86	
    87	### Hooks
    88	
    89	- Hooks implement `CanInterceptAgentLifecycle` and receive/return `HookContext`
    90	- **HookContext** carries state + trigger type + tool data; hooks mutate context (block tools, add errors, emit stop signals)
    91	- Hook categories by convention: Guard hooks (priority 200, run first — check limits), Transform hooks (modify state), Block hooks (prevent tool execution), Decision hooks (policy-based retry/stop/ignore)
    92	- **HookStack** chains hooks in priority order (higher = earlier); immutable — `with()` returns new stack
    93	
    94	### Composition
    95	
    96	- AgentBuilder composes: Tools + Driver + EventEmitter + HookStack + ToolExecutor → AgentLoop
    97	- Many small interfaces (`CanUseTools`, `CanExecuteToolCalls`, `CanInterceptAgentLifecycle`, `CanEmitAgentEvents`) — one role each
    98	- Events are readonly DTOs dispatched via event bus; emitter is a thin wrapper creating event objects from state
    99	- Extend via hooks, not subclassing — AgentLoop is not designed for inheritance (test subclass `TestAgentLoop` is the sole exception)
   100	
   101	# Tests and Quality
   102	
   103	- Use Pest for testing
   104	- Test only services and domain logic, not external dependencies or displayed information
   105	- Before writing tests make sure that the code is easily testable - if not propose refactorings
   106	- Use PHPStan and Psalm for static analysis
   107	
   108	# Build Artifacts
   109	
   110	The `./builds/` directory is **ephemeral** — it is auto-generated and should never be manually edited. Any changes made there will be overwritten on the next build. Always edit source files in `packages/` or `docs/` instead.
   111	
   112	# Development Tools
   113	
   114	- ast-grep - import documentation from: @./notes/tools/AST_GREP.md
   115	- task-master - import documentation from: @./docs-internal/taskmaster.md
   116	- tbd (to-be-done) - issue tracking system, see: @./docs-internal/tbd/tbd_cheatsheet.md
   117	
   118	## `bd` CLI (dense workflow)
   119	**Query**: `bd ready --json` for actionable work; `bd list --json --no-pager` for open issues (`--all` includes closed); `bd show <id> --json` for detail; `bd status --json` for counts/health. Use `bd ready`, not `bd work`. Common filters: `bd ready` supports `-p`/`-t`/`-l`/`--parent`/`--assignee`; `bd list` supports those plus `-s` for stored status.
   120	
   121	**Create**: Task default: `bd create "title" -d "desc" -p 2 -l area:events`; explicit task: `bd create "title" -t task -d "desc" --parent <epic-id>`; epic: `bd create "Epic: title" -t epic -d "goal/context/outcome/acceptance"`; child tasks under epic via `--parent <epic-id>`; dependencies via `--deps "blocks:<id>,discovered-from:<id>"`.
   122	
   123	**Update/Close/Remove**: Claim atomically with `bd update <id> --claim`; update fields/status with `bd update <id> -s in_progress -a <assignee> -p 1 --notes "plan"`; labels: `--add-label`, `--remove-label`, `--set-labels`; close: `bd close <id> -r "done"`; reopen: `bd reopen <id>`; remove (destructive): `bd delete <id> --force`.
   124	
   125	**Dependencies**: use `bd dep <blocker-id> --blocks <blocked-id>` for simple blocker creation, or `bd dep add <blocked-id> <blocker-id>` for explicit dependency management.
   126	
   127	**Migration/health**: current `bd` is Dolt-only. For old repos, preserve `.beads/issues.jsonl` and reinitialize with `bd init --from-jsonl`; validate with `bd doctor --agent --json`; refresh hooks with `bd hooks install`.
   128	
   129	
   130	# Commit Message Guidelines
   131	
   132	- Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) format
   133	- Include a brief description of the change, its motivation, and any relevant issue references
   134	- Never mention CLAUDE in commit messages or code comments
   135	
   136	## Landing the Plane (Session Completion)
   137	
   138	**When ending a work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.
   139	
   140	**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**
   141	
   142	1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create issues for anything that needs follow-up
   143	2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
   144	3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
   145	4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
   146	   ```bash
   147	   git pull --rebase
   148	   git push
   149	   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
   150	   ```
   151	5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
   152	6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
   153	7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session
   154	
   155	**CRITICAL RULES:**
   156	- Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
   157	- NEVER stop before pushing - that leaves work stranded locally
   158	- NEVER say "ready to push when you are" - YOU must push
   159	- If push fails, resolve and retry until it succeeds
   160	
   161	## Git Ownership
   162	
   163	- Leave all git operations to the human user unless explicitly requested.
   164	- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT** - NEVER EXECUTE DESTRUCTIVE GIT COMMANDS WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION.
   165	- Destructive git commands include anything that can discard, overwrite, detach, stash away, or silently replace local work, including `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore`, `git clean`, `git stash`, rebases with conflict-side overwrites, or retrieving older file contents over uncommitted work.
   166	- Before any such command, the agent MUST explain exactly what may be lost or overwritten and make sure the user understands the consequences.
   167	- If there is any risk of losing uncommitted work from the current session or prior user work, stop and ask first.
   168	
   169	<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION -->
   170	## Issue Tracking with bd (beads)
   171	
   172	**IMPORTANT**: This project uses **bd (beads)** for ALL issue tracking. Do NOT use markdown TODOs, task lists, or other tracking methods.
   173	
   174	### Why bd?
   175	
   176	- Dependency-aware: Track blockers and relationships between issues
   177	- Git-friendly: Dolt-powered version control with native sync
   178	- Agent-optimized: JSON output, ready work detection, discovered-from links
   179	- Prevents duplicate tracking systems and confusion
   180	
   181	### Quick Start
   182	
   183	**Check for ready work:**
   184	
   185	```bash
   186	bd ready --json
   187	```
   188	
   189	**Create new issues:**
   190	
   191	```bash
   192	bd create "Issue title" --description="Detailed context" -t bug|feature|task -p 0-4 --json
   193	bd create "Issue title" --description="What this issue is about" -p 1 --deps discovered-from:bd-123 --json
   194	```
   195	
   196	**Claim and update:**
   197	
   198	```bash
   199	bd update <id> --claim --json
   200	bd update bd-42 --priority 1 --json
   201	```
   202	
   203	**Complete work:**
   204	
   205	```bash
   206	bd close bd-42 --reason "Completed" --json
   207	```
   208	
   209	### Issue Types
   210	
   211	- `bug` - Something broken
   212	- `feature` - New functionality
   213	- `task` - Work item (tests, docs, refactoring)
   214	- `epic` - Large feature with subtasks
   215	- `chore` - Maintenance (dependencies, tooling)
   216	
   217	### Priorities
   218	
   219	- `0` - Critical (security, data loss, broken builds)
   220	- `1` - High (major features, important bugs)
